dedupe_keys.name: ls telcom chirplus bc broadcast network planning and coordination software

description: CHIRplus_BC is LS telcom's software for planning and coordinating analogue and digital broadcast networks, combining a geographic information system, a graphical interface, a database and broadcast engineering functions, aimed at regulators managing spectrum and at network operators rolling out transmitters. It offers several interference calculation methods, single frequency network delay optimisation, population analysis, import and analysis of measurements and frequency scans to find usable channels. For international coordination it handles frequency plans, assignments and allotments, supports ITU procedures and agreements such as Geneva 2006, imports data from the ITU BR IFIC and the ITU Digitized World Map, and produces electronic notifications; LS telcom notes that it takes part in several ITU-R study groups. Automatic channel assignment works with raster field-strength calculations or contours, taking account of interference and self-interference, and a multi-threaded network processor plans country-wide single and multi-frequency networks, statistical network gain and compatibility studies such as LTE versus DVB-T. Standards supported include DVB-T2, DVB-T, ATSC 3.0, ISDB-T, DTMB, CMMB, T-DAB and DAB+, HD Radio, DRM, FM and LF, MF and HF, plus 5G Broadcast and LTE-MBMS coverage, and a Visual Basic-like macro language allows unattended runs. Coverage: worldwide. Format and access: commercial software from LS telcom. Caveats: proprietary. Simulation uses: coverage and interference planning of broadcast networks, spectrum re-planning and coverage loss after transmitter failures. Related records: ATDI HTZ Communications is a comparable suite, and BNetzA and BAKOM transmitter data give real networks.
